subject: Private VPC pricing follow-up: reserved commit example & SOW timing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>, Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Private VPC pricing / env count / token volumes

Hi Alex / Lisa - great to speak this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery so we have alignment before I put together a formal pricing summary.

Summary of needs (from today's call):
- Deployment: Private VPC (customer-managed VPC) with a private control plane.
- Environments: three logical environments (prod, staging, dev) with the option to add a DR region.
- Expected token volumes: POC ~5-10M tokens/month; ramp to ~60-80M tokens/month over 6 months if latency & integration look good.
- Key SLOs: 95th percentile token latency target <=120ms; need predictable throughput for batch inference windows.
- Compliance: SOC 2 / audit logs required; KMS integration for keys.
- Contract / procurement: procurement will own T&Cs and SOW; Lisa is the contact.

Open qualification items for pricing:
1) Target unit economics / target $ per 1M tokens you expect for a private deployment (this helps us recommend license vs consumption-heavy model).
2) Number of concurrent environments you want in the initial contract (prod/staging/dev counts as 3; do you want a separate DR?).
3) Desired support tier (Standard business hours vs Enterprise 24/7 + named SLA).
4) Any hard budget bands for annual spend or token-unit spend to guide options.

Attachments: Private_VPC_Pricing_Summary.pdf - a short primer on licensing models we typically propose (license + token overage vs consumption).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the answers above (1-4).
- I'll send a 1-page pricing options sheet (license + support + token tiers) and a draft SOW for procurement to review.
- Optional: a 30-min follow-up with our solutions architect to align on infra & HA requirements.

If it helps, our typical entry point for a customer with your profile is either: (A) annual enterprise license + standard support + per-1M token billing for heavy sustained usage, or (B) reserved capacity (dedicated pools) with a bundled token allowance and an overage price. I'll lay both out once I get your budget target per 1M tokens.

Thanks - talk soon.

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private VPC pricing / env count / token volumes

Thanks Ben - good recap. Answers below inline.

1) Target $/1M tokens: for Private/VPC we're targeting roughly $3,000 per 1M tokens as a ballpark for steady-state economics; for POC we can tolerate higher unit costs but want to see a plan to get to ~3k as volumes ramp.

2) Environments: yes, we need prod + staging + dev (3) initially. We will likely want a DR setup in a second region for prod later (not in initial SOW).

3) Support tier: leaning Enterprise (24/7) due to financial risk - will likely require a named SLA and escalation path.

4) Budget bands: procurement is comfortable with an initial ARR target in the $250k-400k range for year 1 for the Private deployment (license + support + token consumption). That should cover POC + initial ramp if pricing aligns.

Question for you: how do you typically structure license vs consumption for Private installs? Do you do a flat platform license (per environment or per cluster) + per-1M token charge, or a reserved capacity model? Also please include approximate one-time onboarding / integration fees in your breakdown.

I attached our internal cost model (FintechCo_RFP_Response.xlsx) so you can see the token-profile assumptions.

--
Alex Rivera
Head of AI Products | FintechCo
alex.rivera@fintechco.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing follow-up: reserved commit example & SOW timing

Alex - thanks for the details and the model. Per your ask, attached is a reserved-commit example (Reserved_Commit_Example.xlsx) showing blended unit economics at commits inside your $250k-400k ARR band. Quick bullets below so procurement has a one-slide summary.

Reserved commit example (illustrative):
- $275,000/year commit -> includes 55M bundled tokens + Enterprise support (24/7).
- Blended unit cost: ~ $3,000 per 1M tokens at 55M included (overage at $2,500 per 1M).
- Platform license: rolled into the commit (no separate line item).
- One-time onboarding / integration: $30,000 (discounted if included in commit).

Enterprise license + consumption (alternate):
- Platform license: $120,000/year (covers prod/staging/dev).
- Support: $60,000/year for Enterprise tier.
- Token tiers: 0-25M $6,000/1M; 25-100M $3,000/1M; 100M+ custom.
- Onboarding/professional services: $35,000 one-time.

Recommendation: For predictability and to meet your ~$3k target, the reserved-commit example above is cleaner for procurement. It also keeps your ARR inside the band you gave and gives a clear blended cost.

Next steps:
1) I'll send a 1-page pricing options PDF + draft SOW by EOD tomorrow.
2) Marissa will propose 2x 30-min windows for a technical review this week.
3) If procurement wants, we'll prepare a final reserved-commit proposal with contract language for review.

If that works I will attach the 1-pager and SOW draft to the DocuSign template link and loop procurement.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
